summary: Capcom's stylish character-action series, including the numbered games, HD remasters, Special Editions, the Ninja Theory reboot, feature-phone/mobile spinoffs, and current live-service/mobile release.

entries.title: Devil May Cry
entries.definitive_edition: Devil May Cry HD Collection on PC

emulation.emulator: None for primary / PCSX2 for PS2 original
emulation.notes: Use native PC HD Collection; PS2 emulation is only for original-version comparison.

primary.why: The HD Collection preserves the first Devil May Cry with higher-resolution output on modern platforms; PC is the highest-fidelity official route for the original game content.
primary.how_to_play: Play Devil May Cry through Devil May Cry HD Collection on PC/Steam.

entries.remaster_caveats: HD Collection changes presentation/output but does not remake the game.

entries.title: Devil May Cry 2
entries.definitive_edition: Devil May Cry HD Collection on PC

emulation.emulator: None for primary / PCSX2 for PS2 original
emulation.notes: Use native PC HD Collection for the primary.

primary.why: Devil May Cry 2 is included in the HD Collection, making PC the highest-fidelity official route for the complete original DMC2 content.
primary.how_to_play: Play Devil May Cry 2 through Devil May Cry HD Collection on PC/Steam.

entries.remaster_caveats: The HD Collection preserves the original game rather than reworking its design.

entries.title: Devil May Cry: Deadshot

emulation.notes: Practical play depends on preserved handset software/data.

primary.why: Deadshot was a Japanese feature-phone shooter spinoff with no documented modern port, so the original mobile release is the only official version.
primary.how_to_play: Use preserved compatible Japanese feature-phone software/hardware where legally available; otherwise treat as a preservation-only entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: No public modern remake or store release exists.

entries.title: Devil May Cry: Dante X Vergil

emulation.notes: Availability depends on preserved app data and compatible runtime/hardware.

primary.why: One of the 2007-2008 Devil May Cry feature-phone games used DMC3 characters/enemies and is also known as Devil May Cry: Dante X Vergil; no modern port is documented.
primary.how_to_play: Use compatible preserved feature-phone software/hardware where legally available.

entries.title: Devil May Cry 3: Dante's Awakening
entries.definitive_edition: Devil May Cry 3 Special Edition on Nintendo Switch

emulation.emulator: None for primary / PCSX2 for PS2 original
emulation.notes: Use Switch hardware for the primary; PCSX2 only for original PS2 comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Switch complete-content route / PC HD Collection fidelity route

primary.version: Devil May Cry 3 Special Edition for Switch
primary.why: The Switch version is based on Special Edition and adds style-switching, full weapon switching, and local co-op in Bloody Palace, making it the most complete official DMC3 version despite PC HD Collection having a higher display ceiling.
primary.how_to_play: Play Devil May Cry 3 Special Edition on Nintendo Switch; use PC HD Collection only if raw display fidelity matters more than the Switch-exclusive gameplay additions.

secondary.exclusive_content: Higher display/settings flexibility through the HD Collection.
secondary.what_to_play: Use PC HD Collection for a higher-fidelity comparison run if desired.
secondary.why: PC has the better fidelity ceiling but lacks the Switch-exclusive DMC3 features.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Switch version is the complete official gameplay version; PC HD Collection remains useful for display/fidelity preference.

entries.title: Devil May Cry HD Collection
entries.definitive_edition: Devil May Cry HD Collection on PC

primary.why: The 2018 PC release collects Devil May Cry, Devil May Cry 2, and Devil May Cry 3 Special Edition with modern HD output and the highest display/settings flexibility.
primary.how_to_play: Play Devil May Cry HD Collection on PC/Steam.

secondary.exclusive_content: The Switch standalone DMC3 release adds exclusive DMC3 features not present in the HD Collection.
secondary.what_to_play: Use Switch specifically for DMC3's style switching, weapon switching, and Bloody Palace co-op.
secondary.why: The HD Collection is best for the collection package, but Switch DMC3 is the complete DMC3 route.

entries.remaster_caveats: For DMC3 specifically, use the Switch standalone if completeness outranks PC display fidelity.

entries.title: Devil May Cry 4
entries.definitive_edition: Devil May Cry 4 Special Edition on PC

primary.why: Devil May Cry 4 Special Edition adds Vergil, Lady, and Trish as playable characters over the original DMC4; PC is the highest-fidelity official platform.
primary.how_to_play: Play Devil May Cry 4 Special Edition on PC.

entries.remaster_caveats: Original DMC4 is superseded for a full playthrough by Special Edition.

entries.title: Devil May Cry 4 Special Edition
entries.definitive_edition: Devil May Cry 4 Special Edition on PC

primary.why: The Special Edition is the expanded DMC4 release with Vergil, Lady, and Trish playable; PC gives the best fidelity/settings route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Devil May Cry 4 Special Edition on PC.

entries.remaster_caveats: Cataloged separately because it materially expands playable-character content over DMC4.

entries.title: DmC: Devil May Cry
entries.definitive_edition: DmC: Devil May Cry Definitive Edition

emulation.notes: Use native console Definitive Edition for the primary.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PS4/Xbox One Definitive Edition; PC original for raw settings

primary.why: DmC is a separate reboot continuity, and the Definitive Edition adds the upgraded console release content/presentation over the original PS3/360/PC launch.
primary.how_to_play: Play DmC: Devil May Cry Definitive Edition on PS4 or Xbox One; use PC original only if unlocked PC settings matter more than Definitive Edition changes.

secondary.exclusive_content: Native PC settings and high frame-rate flexibility for the original release.
secondary.what_to_play: Use PC for fidelity comparison of the original release.
secondary.why: Definitive Edition has the expanded/retuned package, while PC has raw settings flexibility.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is a reboot/alternate continuity and must not be conflated with the classic storyline.

entries.title: Devil May Cry 5

emulation.notes: Use PS5/Xbox Series X|S hardware for the complete official route; native PC for fidelity comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Special Edition on current consoles / native PC for base build

primary.why: Special Edition adds Vergil and next-gen features/modes including Turbo and Legendary Dark Knight on PS5/Xbox Series X|S, making it the most complete official version even though PC has a higher raw settings ceiling for the base build.
primary.how_to_play: Play Devil May Cry 5 Special Edition on PS5 or Xbox Series X|S; use PC with Vergil DLC only if raw PC fidelity is the priority over Special Edition modes.

secondary.exclusive_content: Highest raw PC settings for the original DMC5 build with Vergil DLC.
secondary.what_to_play: Use PC for a graphics/fidelity comparison run.
secondary.why: PC lacks some Special Edition modes officially, but has the highest hardware-dependent fidelity ceiling.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Switch 2 Devil Hunter Edition is future-dated relative to June 18, 2026 and should be revisited after release.

entries.title: Devil May Cry: Peak of Combat

primary.why: Peak of Combat is the current mobile Devil May Cry action-RPG/live-service entry and is only officially available on mobile platforms.
primary.how_to_play: Install Devil May Cry: Peak of Combat on a compatible iOS or Android device in a supported region.

entries.remaster_caveats: Live-service content, regions, and availability may change.
